definition: Neural machine translation (NMT) is an approach to machine translation that uses an artificial neural network to predict the likelihood of a sequence of words, typically modeling entire sentences in a single integrated model.
details: It is the dominant approach today and can produce translations that rival human translations when translating between high-resource languages under specific conditions. However, there still remain challenges, especially with languages that have less high-quality data available, and with domain shift between the data a system was trained on and the texts it is supposed to translate. NMT systems also tend to produce fairly literal translations.

explainer.lead: Neural machine translation (NMT) uses an artificial neural network to predict the likelihood of word sequences, typically modeling entire sentences in a single integrated model. It is the dominant approach today and can rival human translations for high-resource languages.

tiers.eli5: It's like a super-smart translator that reads a whole sentence and uses its learned experience to write the translation in another language.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers train NMT models on parallel corpora to translate between languages. A pitfall is that performance drops for low-resource languages and domain shifts, and outputs can be overly literal.
tiers.paperLevel: Neural machine translation is an approach to machine translation that uses an artificial neural network to predict the likelihood of a sequence of words, typically modeling entire sentences in a single integrated model. It assigns a probability P(y|x) to potential translations and searches for the most probable one.

explainer.example: An NMT system trained on English-German data can translate 'Hello, world' to 'Hallo, Welt' by predicting the most likely target sequence.
